To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the optimal length of a CO2 gasdynamic laser with a Q-switched resonator is 1.2–1.5 m, and the optimal repetition rate is 10–20 kHz.

the optimal length of the downstream resonator is 2-3 meters for a CO2 mixture with a concentration of 0.5% of CO2 and that the repetition frequency of Q- switching pulses is 1.0-1.5 Hz for a pulse energy of 0.1-1.0 J and a pulse length of 10-20 ns.

the optimum length of the resonator, in the downstream direction is about one meter, that the optimum composition of the mixture is about 20% He + 20% N2 + 60% CO2, and that the optimum repetition frequency is about 10 Hz.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of a new type of gasdynamic CO2 laser, the thermally excited cascade laser, in which a high degree of population inversion is achieved by thermal excitation of the CO2 molecule in a gasdynamic flow, and the laser action occurs on transitions between the vibrational levels of the CO2 and N2 molecules.
the problem of the development of a pulse-periodic cascade gasdynamic CO2 laser with a high repetition frequency of Qswitching pulses.
the possibility of using the CO2 cascade laser as an effective tool for the investigation of the properties of the active medium of gasdynamic lasers.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a cascade laser with a gasdynamic excitation system is a very promising approach for obtaining high power CO2 laser radiation.
the CO2 cascade laser is a powerful tool for studying the properties of CO2 lasers and for developing new laser systems.
, in general, the use of a CO2 cascade laser is not justified in the case of a pulse-periodic regime.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cascade lasers are the most efficient lasers, but they are difficult to design.
we have demonstrated the possibility of using a CO2 cascade laser as a powerful and highly reliable source of radiation in a wide spectral range.
the use of a cascade CO2 laser with an active medium in the form of a gas flow in a channel with a rectangular cross section and with a length of 1-1.5 m is promising.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the use of a CO2 mixture with an increased CO2 concentration in a gasdynamic cascade laser with a short resonator length and a high repetition frequency leads to a significant increase in the energy parameters of the laser radiation.
the optimal repetition frequency depends on the composition of the mixture and the resonator length.
the optimal resonator lengths in the downstream direction and in the direction of the flow are different.
